"""Local person-description continuations, especially noun + 'who'.

Predict a strong positive activation on space-prefixed 'who' immediately
following a person word or an agent-noun ending. Pronouns, punctuation,
capitalization and document starts set weaker or intermediate levels.
Bare 'who', the acronym WHO, 'whose', 'whoever' and French 'qui' have
smaller lexical responses. Selected description words (e.g. 'living' and
'born') also respond after a person noun. Everything else predicts zero.

Only the previous token is remembered, resetting at document boundaries.
This approximates local lexical cues, not grammatical parsing, and leaves
most small background activations unexplained.
"""
READS = ()

# Person nouns and social roles. Plurals use the same class.
PERSON_WORDS = frozenset('''
person individual man woman boy girl child kid infant teenager adult baby
student pupil teacher professor doctor nurse physician patient engineer
worker employee colleague friend relative mother father son daughter
brother sister grandparent wife husband partner member player athlete
author writer poet artist painter performer actor actress singer musician
dancer composer producer director manager businessman leader official
president minister politician researcher scientist scholar educator
professional lawyer judge juror attorney journalist reporter critic analyst
expert customer client user guest visitor resident citizen voter follower
supporter volunteer soldier warrior veteran offender prisoner criminal
victim witness candidate applicant footballer entrepreneur contractor
guy human parent classmate teammate coach assistant officer priest nun monk
ceo senator congressman chairman diplomat pilot immigrant refugee alien
demon elf senior staff alumnus alumni celebrity plaintiff defendant borrower
'''.split())
PERSON_PLURALS = frozenset('people men women children babies elves alumni'.split())
AGENT_SUFFIXES = ('er', 'or', 'ist', 'ian', 'ant', 'ee')
NON_AGENT_WORDS = frozenset('''
other another better older former latter however whether together either
neither after under over number order matter computer center counter
'''.split())
PERSON_DESCRIPTIONS = frozenset('''
born living working walking sitting thinks interested aged experience
training population friendly care welfare health
'''.split())

INDEFINITE_PEOPLE = frozenset('someone somebody anyone anybody'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    prior = previous.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    if word.upper() == 'WHO' and word == word.upper():
        value = 0.76
    elif lower == 'who':
        value = 0.55
        if token.startswith(' '):
            value = 0.50
            if first:
                value = 1.74
            elif prior == 'person':
                value = 2.48
            elif prior in INDEFINITE_PEOPLE:
                value = 2.15
            elif prior in PERSON_WORDS:
                value = 2.18
            elif prior in PERSON_PLURALS or prior.rstrip('s') in PERSON_WORDS:
                value = 1.94
            elif prior == 'those':
                value = 1.50 if previous.strip()[0].isupper() else 1.18
            elif prior in ('one', 'ones', 'him', 'else'):
                value = 1.10
            elif prior in ('everyone', 'everybody', 'others', 'you', 'he', 'she'):
                value = 1.58
            elif prior == ',':
                value = 0.80
            elif prior in ('er', 'or', 'ant', 'ants', 'ian', 'ians'):
                value = 1.35
            elif prior in ('ist', 'ists', 'ers', 'ors', 'ologist'):
                value = 1.75
            elif (len(prior) > 5 and prior not in NON_AGENT_WORDS
                  and prior.rstrip('s').endswith(AGENT_SUFFIXES)):
                value = 1.95
            elif prior in ('know', 'ask', 'see', 'define', 'determine'):
                value = 0.10
            elif previous.strip()[:1].isupper():
                value = 0.90
    elif lower == 'whose':
        value = 0.27
    elif lower == 'qui':
        value = 0.24
    elif lower == 'whoever':
        value = 0.49
    if (prior in PERSON_WORDS or prior in PERSON_PLURALS
            or prior.rstrip('s') in PERSON_WORDS):
        if lower in PERSON_DESCRIPTIONS or lower == 'whom':
            value = 0.55
        elif lower == 'whose':
            value = 0.65
    return (doc, token), value

"""Boundary markers and words for grounds/compounds dominate this approximation.
Document endings are positive; chat endings and tool-call openings are negative.
Gardens, campuses, parks, farms and camps are negative, especially 园/園.
Common compounds and capitalization adjust the lexical response. Other selected
site words and round/group characters have weaker negative responses. Unmatched
tokens are zero. Only document position and the previous token are remembered.
"""
READS = ()

GROUNDS = {'garden': -1.67, 'campus': -1.67, 'farm': -1.2,
           'camp': -1.2, 'park': -0.94}
# Each set is a lexical class, not a list of token ids.
LEXICAL_CLASSES = (
    (-1.5, {'圆', '圓', '团', '團'}),  # Round and group morphemes.
    (-1.5, {'院', '营', 'vườn'}),  # Courtyard/institution, camp, garden.
    (-1.45, {'花园', '公园', '公園', '田园', '家园', '乐园', '幼儿园'}),
    (-2.05, {'校园', '园林'}),  # Campus and landscaped gardens.
    (-2.8, {'园区', '庄园'}),  # Industrial park and estate.
    (-1.0, {'馆', '館', '營', '庄', '莊', '基地'}),
    (-0.74, {'円'}),  # Japanese round/yen character.
    (-0.55, {'원', '厂', '校', '宅'}),
    (-0.3, {'场', '場'}),
    (-1.1, {'gardening', 'campground', '-campus'}),
    (-0.7, {'ranch', 'mansion', 'courtyard', 'garten', 'jardin'}),
    (-0.26, {'school', 'club', 'yard', 'grounds', 'plant', 'plants',
             'hospital', 'town', 'county', 'site', 'facilities'}),
    (-0.45, {'facility', 'plantation', 'stadium'}),
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    position, previous = (0, '') if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else (
        carry[1] + 1, carry[2])
    carry = (doc, position, token)
    decay = 1.0 / (position + 1) ** 0.5
    if token == '<|endoftext|>':
        return carry, 0.89 if position == 0 else 1.60 - 0.44 * decay
    if token == '<|im_end|>':
        if previous in {'</tool_call>', '</tool_response>'}:
            return carry, -0.95 + 0.66 * decay
        return carry, -0.36 if position == 0 else -0.725 + 0.20 * decay
    if token == '<tool_call>':
        return carry, -1.055 + 0.36 / (position + 1)
    if token in {'<think>', '</think>'}:
        return carry, -0.215
    if token == '</tool_response>':
        return carry, 0.22
    if token == '<|im_start|>':
        return carry, -0.04 + 0.125 * decay
    if token == '#' and position == 0:
        return carry, 0.42

    modifier = previous.strip()
    if token in {'园', '園'}:
        # Kindergarten, zoo, and plant-garden compounds weaken the suffix.
        if modifier in {'庭', '幼稚'}:
            return carry, -2.9
        if modifier in {'动物', '動物', '植物'}:
            return carry, -3.5
        if modifier in {'花', '菜', '果', '梅'}:
            return carry, -4.1
        return carry, -4.95 if token == '园' else -4.8
    if token == '院' and modifier.endswith('病'):  # Hospital compounds.
        return carry, -0.83
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word == 'park' and modifier.lower() in {'national', 'car'}:
        return carry, -1.3 if modifier.lower() == 'national' else -0.28
    root = word[:-1] if word.endswith('s') and word != 'campus' else word
    if root in GROUNDS or word == 'campuses':
        value = -1.5 if word == 'campuses' else GROUNDS[root]
        if word != root:
            value *= 0.85
        if root in {'garden', 'campus', 'farm'} and not token.islower():
            value *= 0.8
        if root in {'farm', 'park'} and not token.startswith(' '):
            value *= 0.65
        return carry, value
    for value, words in LEXICAL_CLASSES:
        if word in words:
            return carry, value
    return carry, 0.0

"""Stretch/flex detector.

Fires on words about stretching, flexing, bending and compressing things (elasticity),
most strongly on "stretch" itself and its forms. It types out the current word
(carry), so a word split across tokens ("stre" + "tched") is read whole.

WORDS = {
    "flex": 1.2, "flexed": 1.2, "flexible": 1.2, "flexibility": 1.2, "flexing": 1.2,
    "curved": 0.9, "curvature": 0.9, "curve": 0.15,
    "compress": 0.5, "compressed": 0.7, "compression": 0.5,
    "relax": 0.5, "relaxed": 0.6, "relaxing": 0.5, "relaxation": 0.5,
    "elong": 0.5, "elongate": 0.5, "elongated": 0.5,
    "tension": 0.4, "shrink": 0.4, "stiff": 0.4, "stiffness": 0.4,
    "bend": 0.3, "inflation": 0.7, "inflate": 0.4, "mattress": 0.5,
    "versatile": 0.6, "versatility": 0.45, "squeeze": 0.35,
    "linear": 0.25, "horizontal": 0.2, "flat": 0.2, "slope": 0.2,

CHAR_LEVELS = {"伸": 2.0, "展": 0.8, "屈": 0.9, "弯": 0.5, "扯": 1.0, "牵": 1.0, "张": 0.4, "張": 0.4}

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

"""Approximate rare computing-vocabulary responses in ordinary text.

Computing spellings give negative pulses after prose-like text, even when
used in a nontechnical sense. Recent space-prefixed letters and Chinese
characters raise the prose estimate; programming syntax and fenced code
attenuate the response. Backticks have opening/closing responses, reduced
by recent computing vocabulary. Small formatting offsets cover <think>
and document-initial markers. Other tokens predict zero.

The running frequencies have a memory of roughly sixteen tokens. All
state resets at document boundaries. This captures a coherent rare tail,
not the component's diffuse, smaller token-specific responses.
"""
import re

READS = ()

SERVER_AND_PLATFORM_CUES = (
    'server', 'servers', 'android', 'java', 'api', 'rfc',
    'сервер',
)
SOFTWARE_TERMS = (
    'backend frontend linux unix apache ios python php sql xml json '
    'yaml default syntax serialization console consoles files buffer '
    'native demo permission permissions header headers socket cache '
    'admin redis azure developer developers bash ruby haskell github '
    'windows'.split()
)
RESOURCES_AND_OPERATIONS = (
    'file version versions database databases password passwords '
    'kernel command commands output input variable variables array '
    'arrays debug mobile app apps token tokens cookie cookies host '
    'domain export returned returning execution executed inserted '
    'inserting'.split()
)
CHINESE_OPERATIONS = (
    '返回', '部署', '插入', '交互', '后台', '默认',
    '回调',
)
CHINESE_RESOURCES = (
    '配置', '开发', '版本', '用户', '硬件', '栈',
    '创建', '权限', '代码', '属性', '開發',
)

# One calibrated strength per named word family.
WORD_STRENGTH = {word: strength
    for family, strength in (
        (SERVER_AND_PLATFORM_CUES, 0.656),
        (SOFTWARE_TERMS, 0.279),
        (RESOURCES_AND_OPERATIONS, 0.121),
        (CHINESE_OPERATIONS, 0.555),
        (CHINESE_RESOURCES, 0.245),
    ) for word in family}

FENCE_OPEN = (-0.299, -0.215)
FENCE_CLOSE = (-0.186, -1.115)
INLINE_OPEN = (0.04, -0.26)
INLINE_CLOSE = (0.047, -0.162)

KEYWORDS = set('import package class const var def function public private '
               'void return let null namespace include'.split())
CONTEXT_WORDS = set(WORD_STRENGTH) | KEYWORDS | set(
    'code software program data method type object value class function '
    'argument parameter example'.split())
SYNTAX = re.compile(r'[{};=_\\]|::|->|=>|/\w|\.\w')

# At a document's first token there is no preceding text.
STARTING_MARKERS = {
    '<|im_start|>': .067, '<|im_end|>': .002,
    '<|endoftext|>': .040, '<tool_response>': -.024,
    '<think>': .072, '</think>': .131,
    '`': .132, '```': -.116,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    new_document = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if new_document:
        words, chinese, syntax, computing = 0., 0., 0., 0.
        fenced, inline, previous = False, False, ''
    else:
        _, words, chinese, syntax, computing, fenced, inline, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().casefold()
    ticks = token.count('`')
    prose = min(1., max(0., 4.0 * (max(words, chinese) - .05)))
    if fenced:
        prose *= .2
    confidence = prose * max(0., 1. - 4. * syntax)
    strength = WORD_STRENGTH.get(word, 0.)
    # Ignore Latin fragments joined to the preceding word or identifier.
    joined = (word[:1].isascii() and not token[:1].isspace()
              and previous[-1:].isascii() and previous[-1:].isalpha())
    value = 0. if joined else -strength * confidence
    if ticks:
        marker_confidence = prose * max(0., 1. - 4. * syntax - 4. * computing)
        if ticks >= 3:
            base, slope = FENCE_CLOSE if fenced else FENCE_OPEN
            fenced = not fenced
            inline = False
        else:
            base, slope = INLINE_CLOSE if inline else INLINE_OPEN
            if ticks % 2:
                inline = not inline
        value = base + slope * marker_confidence
    elif token == '<think>':
        value = .15
    if new_document and token in STARTING_MARKERS:
        value = STARTING_MARKERS[token]
    is_word = token.startswith(' ') and word.isalpha()
    is_chinese = any('\u3400' <= c <= '\u9fff' for c in token)
    is_syntax = bool(SYNTAX.search(token)) or word in KEYWORDS
    # Running frequencies, with roughly sixteen tokens of memory.
    words = .94 * words + .06 * is_word
    chinese = .94 * chinese + .06 * is_chinese
    syntax = .94 * syntax + .06 * is_syntax
    computing = .94 * computing + .06 * (word in CONTEXT_WORDS or ticks > 0)
    state = (doc, words, chinese, syntax, computing, fenced, inline, token)
    return state, float(value)

    if word == "甚至":  # Chinese: even.

    if word == ",":

"probably", "today", "now", when that word starts a new clause subject or object

token is a word that starts a clause (determiner or pronoun), predict the adverb's
strength; otherwise 0.

    "today": 0.3,

    "so": 0.3,
    "now": 0.3,
    "maybe": 0.3,

- Everything else: 0.

    core = s.strip().lstrip("-/_")
    return core in ("J", "j") or s.strip() in ("-j", "/j", "_j", "\tj")

    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""

    return None, 0.0

the piece continues the word started by the previous token (no space before it).

space, previous token also letters, same document) and, while the word so far is
3 to 8 letters long, predicts the average activation for such pieces (about 0.013).
Everywhere else it predicts 0.

capitalisation, token identity, position) explain almost none of the variance; the
spike depends on context that the layer-0 attention sees. Negative values are not
modelled.

MAX_WORD_LETTERS = 8

    return piece.strip().isalpha()

    docs = prefix.document_ids

        return carry, 0.0

        j -= 1
        letters += len(pieces[j].strip())

    if continuation and MIN_WORD_LETTERS <= letters <= MAX_WORD_LETTERS:

text, i.e. a blank line ("\\n\\n") or a sentence ending followed by a blank line
(".\\n\\n"), and most strongly after a closing brace, bracket, semicolon or quote
(" }\\n\\n", ";\\n\\n", ")\\n\\n", '"\\n\\n'). It is weaker the further into the
document it is, and it is near zero for a blank line that follows a colon, comma,
question mark or a space. Every other token gets 0.

Why: most of the time this component is quiet; its large activations are almost
all at paragraph breaks. Each program line below states one such fact.

tokens (e.g. " of" and " to" are slightly positive, "using" and " being" slightly
negative) with no simple concept behind it, so this program explains only about a
tenth of the variance on the activations, while predicting 0 elsewhere.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Typical activation of a blank line, by what comes right before it.
BARE = 0.6        # "\n\n" with nothing before it (start of a block)
PERIOD = 0.45     # ".\n\n", end of a sentence
CLOSER = 0.7      # "}\n\n", ")\n\n", ";\n\n", '"\n\n': end of a code or quoted block
CLOSERS = set("};)\"`>")
NOT_A_BREAK = 0.0  # " \n\n", ":\n\n", ",\n\n", "?\n\n": these stay near zero
DECAY = 0.2       # the activation shrinks like (1 + position in document) ** -DECAY


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    # carry = (document id, position within that document)
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        dp = 0
    else:
        dp = carry[1] + 1
    carry = (doc, dp)
    if not token.endswith("\n\n") or "\n" in token[:-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = token[:-2]
    if before == "":
        amp = BARE
    elif before == ".":
        amp = PERIOD
    elif before[-1] in CLOSERS:
        amp = CLOSER
    elif before[-1] in " :,?":
        amp = NOT_A_BREAK
    else:
        amp = PERIOD
    return carry, amp * (1 + dp) ** -DECAY

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    return None, value

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:1459 -- a "Romance -ic adjective" detector.

The component writes a strong NEGATIVE value into the residual stream on the
token that completes a word ending in the spelling -ico, -ica or -ique (and
their plurals -icos, -icas, -iques), as in clínico, técnica, física, unique.
Less strongly it responds to -ici and -iche (Slavic adjectives), to verb forms
in -ifica (verifica), and to a few English/Latin -ic words (technique, economic,
ethical, historic). Place names
that merely end in -ica (America, Africa, Mexico) are ignored, and it is near
zero everywhere else.

The program follows the word being typed: it carries the letters since the
last non-letter (reset at each document start), accents folded away, and reads
the word's ending when each token arrives.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Adjective endings of Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French and Latin spelling.
STRONG_ENDINGS = ("ico", "ica", "ique", "icos", "icas", "iques")
# Weaker endings: Slavic adjectives (-ici, -iche) and the Spanish/Portuguese
# verb forms in -ifica/-ifico (verifica, identifica), which only partly fire.
WEAK_ENDINGS = ("ici", "iche", "ifica", "ifico")
# English and Latin-derived -ic words, with their typical strength.
ENGLISH_IC = {
    "unique": -1.5,
    "symbolic": -1.3,
    "physique": -1.2,
    "critique": -1.1,
    "ethical": -0.8,
    "ethics": -0.8,
    "technique": -0.6,
    "techniques": -0.6,
    "economic": -0.6,
    "numeric": -0.6,
    "historic": -0.4,
    "dynamic": -0.4,
    "antique": -0.4,
}
# Place names ending in -ica, which the component ignores.
PLACE_NAMES = {"america", "americas", "africa", "mexico", "jamaica", "antarctica"}


def _fold(text):
    """Lower case, with accents removed (ática -> atica)."""
    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text.lower())
    return "".join(c for c in decomposed if not unicodedata.combining(c))


def _trailing_letters(text):
    i = len(text)
    while i > 0 and text[i - 1].isalpha():
        i -= 1
    return text[i:][-40:]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the word typed so far, as letters (a string); "" at a row start.
    word = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        word = ""
    word = _fold(_trailing_letters(word + prefix.token_strings[-1]))

    if word in ENGLISH_IC:
        value = ENGLISH_IC[word]
    elif word in PLACE_NAMES:
        value = 0.0
    elif word.endswith(WEAK_ENDINGS):
        value = -0.5
    elif word.endswith(STRONG_ENDINGS):
        value = -2.0
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return word, value

"""Score a local spelling join after a vowel-ending token.

Latin ae/oe joins score negative, au/ai/oi positive. Fallback scores
cover a following non-vowel letter. Related charts cover Cyrillic,
Greek and Arabic letters. Fragment length, neighbouring letters,
accents, iotated Cyrillic vowels, uppercase initials and punctuation
adjust the strength. An isolated e after a uses the short-fragment
strength of a written -ae plural ending. Other positions get zero.
All scores were fitted to training activations. Only the previous
and current token are used, with state reset at document boundaries.
"""
import unicodedata as ud
from collections import namedtuple
from functools import lru_cache

READS = ()
VOWELS = 'aeiou'
# Rows: previous final a/e/i/o/u; columns: next initial a/e/i/o/u.
LATIN = (
    (0.38, -2.70, 1.32, 0.81, 2.14),
    (0.03, 0.08, 0.60, 0.01, 0.37),
    (0.66, 0.64, 0.09, 0.27, 0.20),
    (0.95, -1.44, 1.25, 0.34, 1.22),
    (0.64, -0.19, 0.55, 0.40, 0.69),
)
CYRILLIC_GREEK = (
    (0.21, -0.64, 0.73, 0.47, 1.12),
    (0.19, 0.08, 0.40, 0.08, 0.31),
    (0.55, 0.30, 0.13, 0.22, 0.25),
    (0.71, -0.43, 0.70, 0.21, 0.73),
    (0.61, 0.02, 0.42, 0.18, 0.40),
)
# Arabic vowel letters use a, i and u rows; last column is another letter.
ARABIC = {
    'a': (0.00, 0.00, 0.33, 0.00, 1.06, 0.33),
    'i': (0.12, 0.00, -0.01, 0.00, -0.07, 0.00),
    'u': (0.39, 0.00, 0.21, 0.00, 0.03, 0.13),
}
PREVIOUS_LENGTH = (0.99, 0.86, 1.00, 0.94, 0.79, 0.48, 0.48, 0.18, 0.32)
CURRENT_LENGTH = (1.00, 0.72, 1.00, 0.80, 0.68, 0.47, 0.38, 0.27, 0.25)

GREEK = dict(zip('αεηιουω', 'aeiiouo'))

    'last_vowel last_script first_vowel first_script length '
    'left_gain right_gain isolated_e')


def letter(char):
    if not char:
        return '', -1
    base = ud.normalize('NFD', char.lower())[0]
    if base in VOWELS:
        return base, 0
    if base in CYRILLIC:
        return CYRILLIC[base], 1
    if base in GREEK:
        return GREEK[base], 2
    if base in ARABIC_VOWELS:
        return ARABIC_VOWELS[base], 3
    name = ud.name(base, '')
    for script, label in enumerate(('LATIN', 'CYRILLIC', 'GREEK', 'ARABIC')):
        if label in name and base.isalpha():
            return '', script
    return '', -1

                      if ud.category(c) != 'Mn')

                  else 1.15)
    if len(ud.normalize('NFD', clean[-1:])) > 1:
        left_gain *= 0.36
    if len(ud.normalize('NFD', clean[:1])) > 1:
        right_gain *= 0.58
    if clean[-1:] in 'яюёє':
        left_gain *= 0.58
    if clean[:1] in 'яюёє':
        right_gain *= 0.26
    if start[:1].isupper():
        right_gain *= 0.74
    if start != token:
        right_gain *= 0.19
    length = min(8, sum(c.isalpha() for c in letters))
    right_gain *= CURRENT_LENGTH[length]

                    left_gain, right_gain, token.lower() == 'e')

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    current = spelling(prefix.token_strings[-1])

        previous = carry[1]
        if previous.last_vowel and previous.last_script == current.first_script:
            row = VOWELS.index(previous.last_vowel)
            script = previous.last_script
            if script == 3:
                col = VOWELS.index(current.first_vowel) if current.first_vowel else 5
                value = ARABIC.get(previous.last_vowel, (0.0,) * 6)[col]
            elif current.first_vowel:

                      * current.right_gain)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:1460: a vowel-hiatus detector inside split words.

What it responds to. The tokenizer often cuts a word into short letter pieces, e.g.
"Ha|emat|opota", "ka|uf|mann", "Hu|am|n", "ida|e", "photographia|it". The component is
silent on nearly every token. It lights up when a piece that starts with a vowel letter
continues a word (no space before it, same document) after a piece that ends with a vowel
letter: two vowels meet across a piece boundary.

How big and which sign. A table gives the activation for each vowel pair, indexed by the
vowel that ends the earlier piece (rows) and the vowel that starts the later piece
(columns). The pairs that matter most:
  - earlier piece ends in "a": a later "e" is strongly negative (-2.2, e.g. "Ha|em",
    "ida|e"); a later "u" or "i" is strongly positive (+1.6, +0.9, e.g. "ka|uf").
  - earlier piece ends in "o": a later "e" is about -1.0; "i" +0.8, "u" +0.7.
  - any other vowel pair is small, mostly within +-0.5.
A later piece that starts with a consonant, after an earlier piece ending in "a" or "o",
gets a small positive value (+0.2 after "a", +0.1 after "o"). Everything else predicts 0.

Each table entry is the mean activation over training rows for that vowel pair, so the
program predicts the pair's typical size. It is a simplification: inside a pair the
activation varies a lot (the same pair can be near 0 or large), and the spikes it misses
are mostly in Cyrillic and other non-Latin text.
"""

READS = ()

VOWELS = "aeiou"
# TABLE[earlier piece's last vowel][later piece's first vowel], vowels in the order a e i o u.
TABLE = [
    [0.3, -2.2, 0.9, 0.6, 1.6],
    [0.0, 0.1, 0.4, 0.0, 0.3],
    [0.4, 0.4, 0.1, 0.2, 0.2],
    [0.6, -1.0, 0.8, 0.3, 0.7],
    [0.5, -0.1, 0.3, 0.3, 0.6],
]
# a consonant-initial later piece after a vowel-final earlier piece: small positive mean
CONSONANT_AFTER = {"a": 0.2, "o": 0.1}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    cur = raw.lower()
    value = 0.0
    if prefix.position >= 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
        # the later piece continues a word: no space before it, and both pieces non-empty
        joined = not raw.startswith(" ") and bool(prev) and bool(cur)
        if joined and prev[-1] in VOWELS and cur[0] in VOWELS:
            value = TABLE[VOWELS.index(prev[-1])][VOWELS.index(cur[0])]
        elif joined and prev[-1] in VOWELS and cur[0].isalpha():
            value = CONSONANT_AFTER.get(prev[-1], 0.0)
    return carry, float(value)

The main response is to 'by': supplying, causing, and authoring words boost
it, while recognition and evidential words reverse it. Other linking words
receive smaller negative responses after perception or description words.

fragment, and resets at document boundaries.

    'see seen recognized detected identified verified evidenced'.split()
)
EVIDENCE = set(
    'characterized confirmed indicated known observed assessed approved '
    'inferred apparent understood clear heard'.split()
)
MEASUREMENT = set('determined measured defined denote denoted'.split())
EVALUATION = set(
    'appreciated found evaluated realized analyzed estimated considered reviewed'
    .split()
)
DESCRIPTION = set(
    'represented shown described explained calculated expressed predicted '
    'demonstrated depicted illustrated reflected supported specified named '
    'computed related'.split()
)

# Broad classes share one response rather than a separate score per word.
BY_CLASSES = (
    (RECOGNITION, -2.1),
    (EVIDENCE, -1.3),
    (MEASUREMENT, -0.5),
    (EVALUATION, -0.6),
    (DESCRIPTION, 0.2),
    (set('divided multiplied weighted'.split()), 1.1),  # arithmetic
    (set('obtained achieved accompanied backed captured signed'.split()), 0.5),
    (set('followed divisible step'.split()), 0.35),  # sequence/repetition
    (set('provided offered supplied'.split()), 4.2),  # provision
    (set('caused produced induced released imposed exerted raised'.split()), 3.5),
    (set(  # authorship and publication
        'written created presented sponsored contributed posted made published '
        'prepared drafted filed submitted'.split()), 3.1),
    (set(  # origination, organization, and change
        'developed generated inspired led sold hosted issued increased modified '
        'amended compounded introduced organized operated built'.split()), 2.6),
    (set(  # other agentive actions
        'affected influenced formed driven required done held played conducted '
        'taught served given asked dominated started manufactured sent paid '
        'joined occupied shared composed edited returned'.split()), 2.1),
    ({'and', 'or'}, 0.65),
)
LINKS = {' from', ' in', ' through', ' with', ' if', ' whether',
         ' what', ' how', ' that', ' as', ' using'}


def activation(token, previous):
    if token == ' by':
        for words, response in BY_CLASSES:
            if previous in words:
                return response
        return 1.3 if previous.endswith('ed') else 1.1
    if token.strip() in {'by', 'By'}:
        return 0.75
    if token.strip() in {'From', '_from'}:
        return -0.45
    if token not in LINKS:
        return 0.0
    if previous in RECOGNITION:
        if token in {' from', ' through'}:
            return -1.9
        if token in {' if', ' whether'}:
            return -1.1
        return -0.65 if token in {' what', ' in', ' with'} else -0.35
    if previous in EVIDENCE:
        if token == ' from':
            return -1.5
        return -0.5 if token in {' in', ' with', ' if', ' whether'} else 0.0
    if previous in MEASUREMENT or previous in EVALUATION:
        if token == ' from':
            return -1.1
        return -0.3 if token in {' in', ' with', ' if', ' whether'} else 0.0
    if previous in DESCRIPTION:
        if token == ' in':
            return -0.45
        return -0.25 if token in {' from', ' with', ' using', ' as'} else 0.0
    return 0.0

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = activation(token, previous)
    match = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', previous + token)
    word_fragment = match[0][-60:].lower() if match else ''
    return (doc, word_fragment), float(value)

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:1470 - a "technical word-part" detector.

Reads only the newest token. It responds to a piece of a longer word (a token with no
leading space, letters only) when the piece starts with the letter o (Latin or Cyrillic),
as in "autograph" -> "ograph", "ionosphere" -> "osphere", "discography" -> "ography",
"ecology" -> "ology", "-ogram", "-ometric", "-opathy", "-ocyte". These are Greek/Latin
combining forms of science and technology. The response grows with the length of the
piece (up to 8 letters). Pieces that start with o and then r, n, v, f, w, o or u are mostly
ordinary English words ("one", "our", "out", "or", "over") and get half the response.
Pieces starting with a, e, i, y (4+ letters) get a small response: technical suffixes such
as "-ework", "-iform", "-ectomy", "-alogy". Everything else, including words with a leading
space, scores zero.

Variance explained is about 0.1-0.12: the rule catches the large spikes; the many small
values on ordinary tokens are not modelled.
"""

READS = ()

OPENERS = ("o", "о")            # Latin o, Cyrillic о
WEAK_SECOND = set("rnvfwou")
SUFFIX_STARTS = set("aeiy")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if not piece.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    n = min(len(piece), 8)
    if piece[0] in OPENERS and len(piece) >= 3:
        value = 0.14 * (n - 2)
        if len(piece) > 1 and piece[1] in WEAK_SECOND:
            value *= 0.3
        return carry, value
    if piece.isascii() and piece[0] in SUFFIX_STARTS and len(piece) >= 4:
        return carry, 0.02 * (n - 3)
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 1471 (layers.0.mlp.down_proj:1471).

A weak, diffuse, mostly word-level feature. Plain-terms summary of what it responds to:

- Negative on descriptive words: colours and materials ("a blue", "the wooden", "plastic",
  "steel") and descriptive adjectives ("beautiful", "physical", "delicious", "typical",
  "realistic", "famous"). Other lowercase words ending in -al, -ic, -ous, -ful, -ive, -able,
  -less, -ing get a smaller negative push, and any word right after an article ("the", "a",
  "an") is nudged negative.
- Slightly positive on function-like words ("same", "own", "such", "much", "would", "or").
- Slightly positive on people and kinship nouns ("mother", "father", "staff") and on
  abstract event nouns ("doubt", "danger", "mistake", "investigation").
- Strongly positive on the word that completes a fixed pair opened by a quantifier or by
  "whether"/"either"/"both"/"own"/"also": "both HANDS", "whether OR", "either OF",
  "own RIGHT", "also KNOWN", "both SIDES".

Everything else is near zero. The prediction is the sum of these terms, a hand-set
approximation: on about 1e6 training tokens it explains about 2% of the activation's
variance. The component's activity is spread over thousands of words, so a per-token
lookup table explains far more (about 0.4) but is not a concept, so it is not used here.
"""

READS = ()

COLOUR_MATERIAL = frozenset(
    "red blue green black white yellow purple pink brown gray grey orange golden silver "
    "wooden plastic steel metal glass rubber leather stone cotton silk paper iron gold wood "
    "concrete copper aluminum hardware cloth".split()

    "modern national native natural neutral obvious physical private public rational real "
    "realistic reasonable royal sexual short simple small social southern special straight "
    "strong super trained typical unique valid wild".split()
)

    "mother father husband wife parents staff secretary faculty dog son daughter brother "

    "both either whether all any each every several other also just even still".split()
)

PAIR_COMPLETERS = frozenset("hand hands sides side or of known right rights and".split())
ADJECTIVE_ENDINGS = ("al", "ic", "ous", "ful", "ive", "able", "ible", "less", "ing")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_document = len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and (
        prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
